transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh... hey. I guess I came in because... I'm not really sleeping right anymore. 

I just sort of lie there in the dark. I keep... I don't know, hearing the rain, or just thinking about the bluff giving way. And then when I finally do pass out, I just wake up all sweaty from these dreams. Then I gotta show up to my shift at the call center feeling like I never even went to sleep. So... yeah. That's mainly it.
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're awake and not trying to sleep?

I mean... yeah, I guess. I don't really know about anxious. It's more just... most days, I just feel kinda embarrassed. And... I don't know, scared, I guess. Just under the surface. 

It's stupid, but it just feels like everyone can tell that I messed up. Like they look at me and know I'm not... not as tough as I used to act.
Are there things you used to do that you're avoiding now?

Um... yeah, I guess. 

I just... I don't go near the coast trails anymore. At all. And, uh, my old hiking buddies keep texting me to go out, but I just... I dodge them. I don't answer. 

Just... even thinking about talking to them about going out there... my chest gets all tight. So I just stay away from it.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving a traumatic event?

I guess... sometimes. Yeah. 

Just... stuff pops in my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll just be sitting at my desk with my headset on, and suddenly I hear the sound of the rocks sliding. Or I can feel my leg stuck under me again. And just for a minute, it's like... I'm not at work. I'm just right back out on that trail.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts about what happened on the trail?
I mean... yeah. I guess. I try not to think about it. I just try to keep busy with work, mostly. Keep my head down. But... yeah. I don't really want to dwell on it.
Do you feel guilty about what happened on the trail?

Yeah. I mean... I shouldn't have been out there alone. It was stupid. Just... careless. 

And now... I don't know, it's just hard to relax. Anywhere, really. Like if I stop paying attention, something else is going to go wrong.
Are there things you used to enjoy doing that you no longer find interesting?
No... not really. I mean, I still do the same stuff I usually do. Just... play games or whatever. I don't think that's changed.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself?
Uh... no. Not really. I don't think I've ever felt like that.
Do you ever feel numb or detached from the world around you?
No... I don't think so. I don't really feel numb. Just... I don't know, just regular, I guess. I don't feel disconnected or whatever.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
Um... about four months, I guess. Ever since I got... trapped, after that bluff trail collapsed.
How often do you think about what you could have done differently to prevent the trail collapse?

Um... pretty often, I guess. I just... I keep thinking about how stupid I was. Like, just careless for being out there by myself. And... I don't know. Now it just feels like if I let my guard down anywhere, something bad is gonna happen. So... yeah.
How often do you think about the people you feel you've let down or disappointed because of what happened on the trail?
I don't... really think about that. I mean, I was by myself out there, so... I didn't really let anyone else down. Just... yeah, I don't really have thoughts like that.
How often do you think about being responsible for what happened on the trail?

Um... I guess I already said this, but... yeah, a lot. I just... I keep thinking I was stupid. Careless, you know? Just... being out there alone. And... I don't know, now it just feels like... if I let my guard down, anywhere... something bad is going to happen. So... yeah. I think about it a lot.
How often do you think about what you could have done to prevent the trail collapse and feel guilty about it?

Um... I don't really know what else to say. I mean, I couldn't have stopped the actual trail from falling. I just... like I already told you, I just feel stupid for going out there in the first place. That's... that's all, really.
Have you noticed a decrease in how much you enjoy the things you used to like doing since the trail collapse?
Um... no, not really. I still do the same stuff I used to. It's... it's about the same, I guess.
How often do you think about what happened on the trail and wish you had done something differently?
Um... I don't know. Like I said, I just... I wish I hadn't gone out there. That's about it. I don't really think about doing anything else differently.
How many activities or places have you been avoiding since the trail collapse?

Um... I don't really have a number. I just... I won't go near the coast trails now. And, uh... I guess I kind of dodge texts from my hiking buddies. Just... even talking about going out there makes my chest tighten up. So... yeah. I just avoid them.
How many times a week do you think about going to the coast trails but decide not to?
Um... I don't know. I don't really keep track. I just... I don't go.
